steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl.
Beat butter and sugar with an electric mixer in a medium bowl until fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in flour mixture in two batches, then stir in chocolate chips and walnuts.
Roll or scoop dough into walnut-sized balls and place 1 1/2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets. Press on each cookie slightly to flatten.
Bake in the preheated oven until light golden brown, 15 to 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven and transfer to wire racks to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Chip Shortbread Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These buttery chocolate chip shortbread cookies are rich, delicious, and irresistible! Make the dough ahead, freeze, and bake when ready.

video.description: Two great flavors combine in one extraordinarily tasty cookie! Pure flour, butter, sugar and salt come together to make a classic shortbread dough, then walnuts and semisweet chocolate join in to take the great taste to legendary status. You’ll love how the dough freezes well for satisfaction when you want it, or just freeze up dough ahead and when you need a holiday tray, you’re ready to bake. Dough is also receptive to the whims of your own mix-in favorites, such as crushed toffee bar or peppermint candy.

review.reviewBody: This is a delicious, crisp, buttery, chocolately cookie! I used salted butter because that is what I had. I didn't have any nuts, so I didn't use them either. Despite these changes the cookies were still wonderful! The cookies looked raw after baking them 25 minutes, but I took them out anyway and put them on the cooling rack. After about 15 minutes, they were crisp and still warm. My husband brought some to his friends at work and they loved them! I plan on doubling the recipe next time :)

I baked this New Years eve , boy, was it the BEST shortbread recipe I have ever made, and sooooooo simple too.

I didn't bake traditional cookie style, as indicated in the recipe. I placed the entire dough in a round spring pan, and voila! I did add pure almond extract, and because I baked it pie-like, the baking time was longer. But all worth it! Heat the finish product at 10-15 seconds, and add a scoope or 3 of vanilla ice cream.....HOLY MACKINAW....heaven in my mouth!

See picture attached. This will be my go-too shortbread recipe!

Incredibly easy and delicious! Made per instructions first time with added 1/2 tsp of vanilla-wonderful! 2nd batch tried the 1/4 cup brown and white sugar with 1/2 tsp almond extract- also increased oven to 350—mind blowing! Love the recipe Tina!! This will become a staple.

Just baked these. They are as amazing as most reviews say, very rich and delicate. I added a T of orange zest because I love chocolate and orange together. The only reason I gave them 4 stars instead of 5 is that I think the baking time is off. If you chill this dough (and you should as it is very soft and buttery), you need to bake at least 25 minutes @ 300. I'd even go 30 next time, as at 25 they still were very pale.

I made this and it turned out perfectly! I made a few tweaks to the recipe though: - pulsed the sugar to make it finer (or you could just use powdered or castor sugar). - added nutmeg and cinnamon and left out the walnuts. - baked it at 170 degrees for 20 min. Also it’s worth noting that these need to be transferred to a cooling rack and cooled slightly to hold its shape.

Best choc chip cookie recipe ever!!

Absolutely delicious, crumbly and buttery!
 
After reading a couple of reviews that complained about the cookies being too crumbly, I made my first batch cautiously on Christmas eve with no modifications. The cookies came out very crumbly but they were still a big hit.

For the 2nd and 3rd batches, I doubled the recipe then added ONE egg, Vanilla extract, substituted 1/3 of the flour with Almond flour, and replaced the walnuts with flaked almonds.
The result was an incredible, delicate-tasting cookie! 
I believe I have just found my go-to Chocolate Chip Cookie recipe!
p.s. The taste and texture definitely do improve when made a day ahead of serving.
Easy, great recipe. Make sure they cool down for awhile before you eat them. I made cookie bars in a 13x9 glass cake pan. Semi sweet chocolate chips work great in this recipe.

OMG! This is the best. I wish I had known about this recipe long time ago. I have tried in the past but shortbread never worked ( maybe because I used margarine instead of butter?).Used butter this time ( salted, unsalted not avail so I omitted the salt) I used brown sugar ( had no white) and Nestle Morsels and More ( choc morsels, carmel bits and peanut halves). These cookies are so amazing. Thank you for the recipe. It's saved now.

This is a great recipe. Tried to look for something similar on other sites but so far haven't found any. Increased the serving size to 27 servings. Omitted chocolate chips and walnuts and instead added the same qty of chopped pecans. Added almond and vanilla extract. Shaped dough into a log and chopped into rounds, laid out on cookie sheet and baked at 300F as called for and rotated pans halfway. Cooled ~1 min on pan after baking then transferred with spatula onto wire rack to prevent crumbling. The log technique helped, but I wish I could find a still better way to keep the form of the cookies cylindrical. My mother calls it "Sandies" like the Keebler brand cookies and periodically asks for them.

Excellent recipe. After reading several reviews I made the recipe, the only change I made was to add a little vanilla extract. Honestly, it probably didn’t need the addition. I beat the butter and sugar until very very fluffy, or as another reviewer put it, “beat within an inch of its life”.
I found the dough to be a bit crumbly but it comes together nicely when you mix in the chips by hand as well as forming the balls by hand. The warmth of your hands helps the butter meld in with the dry ingredients. 
Just as an experiment, I left 1/3 of the dough plain, added finely chopped pecans to 1/3, and mini-chocolate chips the the other 1/3. Then I baked them as directed. 
At first I thought they were awful and I planned to toss them all out. I waited until the next day and boy am I glad I did! The flavors had a chance to blend overnight and they are incredible! Addictive too and not overly sweet. In fact, the pecan ones remind me of the Keebler brand pecan sandies. 
It didn’t make a huge batch, maybe 2 dozen 1-1/2 cookies.. Thats probably a good thing too, as I’ve eaten all but one of them myself! 
This is a definite keeper! Thanks for the post ??

This is almost the exact 70 plus-year-old cookie recipe I have from my mother. We replaced the chocolate with as many nuts.
I love chocolate but not with this cookie, try without. The only diff was 1 t. of vanilla and 1 t. of water. The water helps spread the cookie.
Mix butter and sugar for at least 15 minutes. If you make with just the nuts, roll in powdered sugar after cooling.

First time making these cookies. I was looking for a recipe after having this cookie at a bakery in Carson City Nevada ( Paul Shats). This cookie is really close to Shats bakery in cookie. Easy to make and followed recipe as written.
Its yummy good. They turned out great. Even without eggs!!! Cheers
It's great fully recommend

Big mistake no egg makes cookies complete crumble disaster.What a waste of ingredients and time also no vanilla why didn’t I listen to my inner amateur chef and add the necessary egg to hold this together. I trusted you and was let down.

These have been a family staple for many years back when they were still posted as "Tina's" chocolate chip shortbread cookies. We sub the chocolate chips for a full size hazelnut chocolate bar from Aldi. We dice it up and use it just as directed. Thanks for this family staple Christmas time recipe!
I used mini chocolate chips and refrigerated the dough before baking. Delicious cookie!!!
So easy and so Good! I made the first batch like recipe and added a bit of vanilla. 2nd batch I added all the original ingredients then chopped pecans and milk chocolate chips. Yum
These are exceptionally delicious! I made these exactly as the recipe and ended up with three dozen. Will definitely make these again!
We did not enjoy this cookie. This is not a true shortbread cookie. Much prefer shortbread with powdered over granulated sugar.
